exposure: Intravenous ketamine/esketamine administration during cesarean section (various dosage regimens and forms)
Prenatal features (Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale (EPDS) score, thoughts of self-injury, bad mood during pregnancy)
outcome: Efficacy of ketamine/esketamine in preventing postpartum depression (PPD)
cohort: The study included 507 women who received ketamine/esketamine intervention during cesarean section.
finding: Prenatal EPDS score >= 10, thoughts of self-injury, and bad mood during pregnancy were associated with poorer ketamine efficacy, while a high dose of esketamine (0.25 mg/kg loading dose+2 mg/kg PCIA) was the most effective regimen and esketamine was generally recommended over ketamine for PPD prevention.
mod_finding: The study specifically investigated the efficacy of ketamine/esketamine administered during the course of cesarean section for PPD prevention, linking the intervention directly to this mode of birth.
